name: Transport for London
body: A meta description on every page read, framing denied, one-year HSTS, a canonical, and a sitemap. But /.well-known/security.txt answers 404, so a researcher who finds a flaw has no published contact.
lesson: Publish /.well-known/security.txt with Contact and Expires lines. It takes minutes.
summary: tfl.gov.uk scores 86 out of 100 (B). 0 checks fail now, 22 are at risk, and 18 pass. Fix first: 13 sitemap URLs point at another host or scheme.

fix.title: 13 sitemap URLs point at another host or scheme
fix.evidence: In /sitemap.xml: an unreadable URL (13). The sitemap should list only URLs on https://tfl.gov.uk.
fix.fix: Regenerate the sitemap with the production https host.

fix.title: No content security policy
fix.evidence: content-security-policy was absent on the start page. Missing on all 19 pages read. Injected scripts are not limited by the browser.
fix.fix: Start with the Report-Only policy in the fix kit, watch the reports for a week, then enforce it.

fix.title: X-Content-Type-Options is not sent
fix.evidence: Browsers may guess a file's type and run it as script. Missing on all 19 pages read.

fix.title: Referrer-Policy is not sent
fix.evidence: Browsers fall back to their default. An explicit policy keeps full URLs from leaking to other sites. Missing on all 19 pages read.

fix.title: Permissions-Policy is not sent
fix.evidence: Embedded content can ask for the camera, microphone, or location. Missing on all 19 pages read.

fix.title: 18 pages have no canonical link
fix.evidence: /fares/, /help-and-contact/, /maps, /plan-a-journey/ and 14 more. Without it, tracking parameters and trailing slashes can split ranking signals.
fix.fix: Add <link rel="canonical" href="…"> with the page's own https URL.

works.title: AI answer and search crawlers may read the start page
Plain http redirects permanently to https
Every image has an alt attribute
The start page arrived in 332 ms
Every page has a meta description
